Implementation Plan ## Implementation plan: profile-aware consumer drift audit Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends ConsumerDriftAuditor._run_gh_api / _load_profile_manifest_names Scope-mode justification: The issue spells out a bounded change to `scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py`, its existing test, and two doc fragments. It reuses the auditor's existing retry wrapper (`_run_gh_api`), its 404 classifier (`_is_not_found_response`) and its per-repo cache pattern (`workflow_dir_listing_cache`). Nothing in the workflow, CLI flags, summary JSON or dataclass fields needs to change. Under the Boil the Lake rule the complete version costs only a few lines more than a shortcut, so the plan also covers the fail-safe paths (unknown profile, unreadable manifest). §6 ranks correctness above speed, and without those paths the audit could under-report drift. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py` - `tests/test_audit_consumer_drift.py` - `changelog.d/drift-audit-profile-aware.md` (new) - `agents.d/-drift-audit-profile.md` (new; the implementer fills in this issue's number) ## Functions or modules to implement All in `scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py`. Every change adds something; no existing identifier is renamed or removed. 1. **Constants.** Add `WORKFLOW_PROFILE_NAMES = ("core", "standard", "full")`, `DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_PROFILE = "full"` and `UNKNOWN_WORKFLOW_PROFILE = "unknown"`. Check first that these names are free in the module. 2. **`_load_named_profile_manifest_names(templates_dir: Path, profile: str) -> set[str] | None`** (new helper, placed next to `_load_profile_manifest_names`). - Reads `templates_dir / "profiles" / f"{profile}.txt"` and applies the same line filters as today: comments and blank lines skipped, `/`, `\`, `.` and `..` rejected, `PROFILE_MANIFEST_NAME_RE` applied. - Returns `None` when the profile is not one of the three known names, or when the file is missing or unreadable (`OSError`, `UnicodeDecodeError`). Callers read `None` as "no manifest, keep today's behaviour for this profile", which keeps it distinct from an empty set. - `_load_profile_manifest_names` keeps its exact body and contract: it still returns an empty set on failure. It is not refactored to call the new helper, so §10 holds and its existing tests are untouched. 3. **`load_profile_manifests(templates_dir: Path) -> dict[str, set[str]]`** (new). - Returns `{profile: names}` for each profile whose helper result is not `None`. - A profile missing from the dict falls back to today's behaviour. 4. **`ConsumerDriftAuditor.__init__`** gets a new keyword-only parameter `profile_manifests: dict[str, set[str]] | None = None` and two new attributes: - `self.profile_manifests` stores the parameter. - `self.workflow_profile_cache: dict[str, str] = {}` holds the per-repo cache, following the `workflow_dir_listing_cache` pattern. - With the default `None`, profile resolution is off: no API call, the profile reads `unknown`, and behaviour is identical to today. Every existing caller and test keeps its exact call sequence. 5. **`ConsumerDriftAuditor.fetch_workflow_profile(self, repository: str) -> str`** (new). - If `self.profile_manifests is None`, return `"unknown"` without calling the API. - Otherwise check the cache first. On a miss, call `GET repos//actions/variables/WORKFLOW_PROFILE` through `self._run_gh_api(endpoint)`, which handles the `application/vnd.github+json` accept header and transient retries. - Add a §14 comment directly above the call. It must say: one extra REST read per consumer per run; the existing calls (the `contents/.github/workflows` listing and the per-file raw content reads) return no repository variables; the result is cached per repository; and every failure falls back to `unknown` (fail safe). - Result mapping: - `returncode == 0` → parse JSON, take `.value` if it is a string, then `.strip().lower()`. A value in `WORKFLOW_PROFILE_NAMES` is returned as is; anything else (including an empty value) gives `unknown`. - `returncode != 0` and `_is_not_found_response(...)` → `full`, because an unset variable means `full`, matching `update_workflows.yml`. - Any other failure, or bad or non-object JSON → `unknown`. - This method never raises, so a repo with an unreadable variable is still audited exactly as today. 6. **`ConsumerDriftAuditor.audit_repository`** changes: - Call `profile = self.fetch_workflow_profile(repository)` first. Then print `DRIFT_SCAN_START repository= templates= profile=

`; the new field is appended at the end. - Set `profile_names = self.profile_manifests.get(profile) if self.profile_manifests is not None and profile != "unknown" else None`. - In the loop, before fetching content: if `profile_names is not None and file_name not in available_files and file_name not in profile_names`, print `DRIFT_SCAN_SKIP repository= file= reason=not_in_profile profile=

` and `continue`. - The condition is "not in the directory listing", which is the same test `fetch_workflow_content` uses to return `None` without a fetch. - A file the consumer has is always fetched and compared, so out-of-profile drift is still reported. - Everything else is unchanged: the `DriftItem` and `RepoAuditResult` fields, the outcome rules, and the `DRIFT_SCAN_DIFF`, `DRIFT_SCAN_OK` and `DRIFT_SCAN_ERROR` lines. 7. **`main()`** builds `profile_manifests = load_profile_manifests(args.templates_dir)` and passes it to `ConsumerDriftAuditor(...)`. No CLI flag changes, and no change to `.github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml`, which already sets `GH_TOKEN` from `secrets.GH_PAT` with `repo` scope. ## Data structures affected - `ConsumerDriftAuditor` gains the optional constructor kwarg `profile_manifests` and the attribute `workflow_profile_cache`. - `DriftItem`, `RepoAuditResult` and the summary JSON (`summarize_results`) are unchanged. Skipped templates show up only in the logs. ## API or interface changes - **New GitHub REST read:** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/variables/WORKFLOW_PROFILE`, once per consumer per run and cached. Its response is an object with `name`, `value`, `created_at` and `updated_at`. An unset variable returns 404. - **Log lines:** a new `DRIFT_SCAN_SKIP` prefix, plus a `profile=` field appended to `DRIFT_SCAN_START`. - **Python API:** an optional kwarg and new functions only. `load_expected_templates` and `_load_profile_manifest_names` are unchanged. ## Decisions ### D1 — Profile resolution is opt-in through a constructor kwarg - Chosen: `profile_manifests=None` turns resolution off (no API call, `profile=unknown`, today's behaviour). `main()` always passes the loaded manifests. - Alternatives considered: always fetch the variable inside `audit_repository`; that would require adding a planned variables call to every existing FakeExecutor test. - Why: existing callers and the ordered FakeExecutor tests keep their exact call sequences (§10 backward compatibility), while production always resolves the profile. ### D2 — Fetch the profile before `DRIFT_SCAN_START` - Chosen: fetch the profile first, then print the start line with `profile=`, then list the directory. - Alternatives considered: fetch lazily, only when a template is missing from the listing (fewer calls, but the start line could not carry the profile). - Why: the issue requires `profile=` on `DRIFT_SCAN_START`, and the fetch cannot raise, so the order does not affect error handling. ### D3 — Unknown profile or missing manifest falls back to today's behaviour - Chosen: a non-404 failure, an invalid value, or an unreadable `profiles/

.txt` means no skipping. - Alternatives considered: treat an unknown profile as `core` (smallest) or as `full`. - Why: failing safe means reporting more drift, never less, as the issue requires. ### D4 — New manifest loader added alongside the old one - Chosen: a new `_load_named_profile_manifest_names` returning `None` on failure. The old full-only function is left untouched. - Alternatives considered: give `_load_profile_manifest_names` a `profile` parameter, or have it delegate to the new helper. - Why: §10 naming immutability, the existing tests pin its behaviour, and the new helper needs a distinct "no manifest" result. ## Security considerations - **Trust boundaries:** the consumer's variable value is untrusted input from the consumer repo. It is stripped, lower-cased and checked against a fixed allowlist. It is never used to build a filesystem path (only the three known profile names reach the `profiles/

.txt` lookup), and only the allowlisted value or the literal `unknown` appears in logs. - **Authorization:** no new surface. The read uses the existing `GH_TOKEN` (GH_PAT, `repo` scope). Variable values are not secrets, but the plan still logs only the normalised allowlisted value, never raw response bodies, for the profile. - **Abuse cases:** - A consumer sets `WORKFLOW_PROFILE=../../x` or a long string → `unknown`, and full auditing applies. - A consumer sets `core` to hide drift in a `full` wrapper it actually has → that file is still compared and reported; only absent files are skipped. This matches the updater, which would not install those wrappers for that profile anyway. - A token with no variable access (403) → `unknown`, the fail-safe result. - No money paths are touched. Failure modes: - Variables endpoint returns 403/5xx after retries → profile `unknown`; the audit runs as today and shows more drift. Recovery: none needed. - A manifest file is missing on the templates checkout → that profile is absent from `profile_manifests`, so there is no skipping for consumers on it. - A malformed JSON response → `unknown`. ## Risks and edge cases - **404 ambiguity:** a 404 can also mean the token cannot see the repo.
